meta.title: Dan Patrick, 9 days of posts
meta.subject: Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick (R), running for re-election against Rep. Vikki Goodwin (D), election Nov 3, 2026
meta.subtitle: Oct 6 to Oct 14, 2026. Each dot is one post with 1K+ views mentioning Dan Patrick, plus every post repeating an earlier one, in the lane for what it argues. Higher and bigger means more views. White means 90% or more the same words as an earlier post, with a white line back to it. Coloured lines link a post to the post it quoted or replied to. Updated daily.

lanes.label: Goodwin: Austin liberal tax-lover
lanes.description: Patrick and allies portray Vikki Goodwin as an Austin liberal who loves taxes (income, gas, death), would defund the police, and backs rogue DAs.

lanes.label: Patrick's conservative record and Trump alliance
lanes.description: Patrick promotes himself as a proven conservative who passed school choice, cut red tape and backed tougher bail laws, standing with Trump, Paxton and Texas Republicans to keep Texas red.

lanes.label: Patrick: church-state and culture-war extremism
lanes.description: Critics say Patrick is a culture warrior pushing Christian nationalism and censorship, citing his claim that separation of church and state is a lie, his push to ban books such as Night, and his flag/socialism rhetoric.

lanes.label: Patrick tied to Paxton scandals
lanes.description: Attacks tie Patrick to Ken Paxton's baggage, including the claim that he took a payoff while presiding over Paxton's impeachment trial, and say Republicans are abandoning the ticket.

lanes.label: Patrick vulnerable: polls and odds
lanes.description: Posts present polls and betting odds showing Goodwin leading or close and Patrick underperforming Abbott, framing the Lt. Gov. race as a real Democratic pickup chance.

lanes.label: Goodwin: hemp voters and pragmatic alternative
lanes.description: Goodwin is presented as a policy-minded, bipartisan legislator who can beat Patrick, including by mobilizing hemp users angry about the THC ban.

lanes.label: Pushback
lanes.description: Posts doubting, mocking, fact-checking or arguing against the dominant narratives.

Banning books like Night robs students of the opportunity to learn where hatred, antisemitism and dehumanization can lead. Whose interests are being served by keeping students in the dark about history’s darkest chapters? And what exactly are we teaching students when we make human suffering off-limits?
